rows.assessment_method: physicians' clinical assessment by two independent dermatologists (blinding and how the two ratings were combined not in abstract); patients' overall satisfaction
rows.time_from_start: Two months after a single treatment [start and final treatment are the same single session]

rows.arm_result: more than 50% improvement compared with baseline in 36 patients (90%) at two months after the single treatment
rows.patient_noticeability: not in abstract (spot noticeability not reported); overall satisfaction: 33 patients (82.5%) very satisfied or satisfied with one session [denominator 40 inferred from 33/40 = 82.5%]
rows.dark_overshoot: postinflammatory hyperpigmentation in 'a few patients' (number not in abstract); resolved spontaneously within 2 months after the assessments
rows.texture_or_scar: not in abstract for scarring or texture; long-standing erythema in 'a few patients' (number not in abstract), resolved spontaneously within 2 months after the assessments; 'No other noticeable side effects were observed'
rows.uncertainty: Abstract only. 'More than 50% improvement' is partial repigmentation, not complete coverage or colour match; the grading scale is not given. Only one efficacy time point, 2 months after the single treatment, far short of six months; no later efficacy visit is reported, although side effects were followed for up to 2 months after the assessments [about 4 months after treatment]. No control arm, so spontaneous change cannot be excluded. Mostly facial lesions, while the authors note the extremities are the most frequently affected areas in IGH, so the sample may not represent typical IGH. Gender ratio printed as '7 : 33' without saying which sex is which. Mean age 57.5 ± 10.9 years. Lesion counts, lesion size, laser settings and Fitzpatrick types not in abstract. Patient-level result; how per-lesion outcomes were combined into a patient score is not stated. Denominators for 90% and 82.5% are not printed [both fit 40].
rows.citation: Shin J, Kim M, Park SH, Oh SH. The effect of fractional carbon dioxide lasers on idiopathic guttate hypomelanosis: a preliminary study. J Eur Acad Dermatol Venereol 2013;27(2):e243-e246 (Epub 2012 May 31)

quotes.quote: A total of 40 patients with IGH were enrolled.
The hypopigmented lesions were treated using a 10 600-nm carbon dioxide fractional laser (CO(2) FL).
Two months after a single treatment, physicians' clinical assessments were performed and the patients' overall satisfaction was evaluated.
Two months after a single treatment, physicians' clinical assessments were performed
Two months after treatment, objective assessments performed by two independent dermatologists indicated more than 50% improvement in 36 patients (90%), compared with baseline.
33 patients (82.5%) were very satisfied or satisfied with just one session of CO(2) FL treatment.
Although a few patients complained of long-standing erythema and postinflammatory hyperpigmentation, these problems spontaneously resolved within 2 months after the assessments.
Although a few patients complained of long-standing erythema and postinflammatory hyperpigmentation, these problems spontaneously resolved within 2 months after the assessments.
No other noticeable side effects were observed.
The face was the most commonly treated area, although the extremities are epidemiologically the most frequently affected areas.
The mean age of enrolled patients was 57.5 ± 10.9 years and the gender ratio was 7 : 33.
Yonsei University College of Medicine, Seoul, Korea

verifier.notes: Verifier 1, 2026-11-27, source papers/excerpts/shin2013.txt (PubMed abstract). 2 failed cells. (1) row 1 (index 0), patient_noticeability: record is ABSTRACT_ONLY, so the parenthetical '(spot noticeability not reported)' uses the full-text term; source is the abstract only, so it should read 'not in abstract' throughout. (2) row 1 (index 0), uncertainty: source says 'a few patients complained of long-standing erythema and postinflammatory hyperpigmentation, these problems spontaneously resolved within 2 months after the assessments', i.e. erythema and hyperpigmentation were still present at the 2-month efficacy assessment and may have affected the improvement grading; uncertainty does not record this. All other cells, quotes, analysis_unit (patients), time_from_last_treatment (2 months after the single treatment) and outcome_tier (partial_repigmentation) match the source.
